summary.name: Firefox
summary.one_liner: Firefox is a free, open-source web browser from Mozilla that blocks trackers by default and emphasizes privacy and user control.
use_cases: switching browsers and importing bookmarks and passwords
watching video while working in other tabs
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Firefox as a browser that blocks trackers automatically with no setup needed. It offers tab groups, Firefox View, and pinned tabs for organizing many tabs. Reader mode strips distractions from articles, and picture-in-picture keeps video visible while browsing. A customizable sidebar and AI features that users can turn on or off are also mentioned. When switching, bookmarks, passwords, and history can be brought over automatically. The page states that Mozilla does not sell personal data.
notable: Blocks trackers automatically with no setup
AI features are optional and can be turned off entirely
Imports bookmarks, passwords, and history from other browsers
caveats: Platform list is not stated on the page beyond the web; desktop and mobile availability is not confirmed here
The awesome-mac listing describes it as open source, but the page text itself does not say so
